claim: Tessellate CLI can export reports as CSV.

passages.text: Tessellate CLI generates usage reports for your workspace.
Run `tessellate report --format csv` to write the report as comma-separated values instead of the default JSON.
Install Tessellate with Homebrew or download a binary from the releases page.
Reports include seats, storage and API calls for the selected billing period.

claim: Quillstack's free tier includes custom domains.

passages.text: Quillstack is a hosted publishing platform for documentation sites.
Custom domains are available on paid plans only; sites on the free tier are served from a quillstack.app subdomain.
The free tier includes unlimited pages and up to three editors.

claim: The Brightwave SDK retries failed requests automatically.

passages.text: The Brightwave SDK exposes a `timeout` option on every request, in milliseconds.
Errors are raised as BrightwaveError with the HTTP status code and the request id.
Brightwave's REST API returns JSON and uses standard HTTP status codes.
You can pass a custom fetch implementation to the client constructor.

claim: The Lumen API allows 1,000 requests per minute per key.

passages.text: Rate limit: 100 requests per minute per API key. Contact sales if you need a higher limit.
When you exceed the limit the API responds with 429 and a Retry-After header.
Lumen keys are created in the dashboard under Settings → API.

claim: The Lumen API allows 100 requests per second.

passages.text: Rate limit: 100 requests per minute per API key. Contact sales if you need a higher limit.
When you exceed the limit the API responds with 429 and a Retry-After header.

claim: Nimbus Queue delivers messages in FIFO order.

passages.text: Nimbus Topics delivers messages in FIFO order within a partition.
Nimbus Queue supports visibility timeouts of up to 12 hours.
Both Nimbus Queue and Nimbus Topics are billed per million requests.

claim: Orbital DB's latest release is version 5.2.

passages.text: October 14, 2026 — Orbital DB 5.2 is now available, our newest release, with faster vector indexes.
June 3, 2026 — Orbital DB 5.1 is now available with logical replication.
Orbital DB is an open-source document database written in Rust.

claim: Kestrel Agent runs on Windows.

passages.text: Kestrel Agent supports Linux and macOS. Windows is not supported.
The agent uses about 40 MB of memory and ships as a single binary.
Kestrel's dashboard works in any modern browser, including on Windows.

claim: All Fernway plans include single sign-on.

passages.text: Single sign-on (SAML and OIDC) is included in the Fernway Enterprise plan.
Fernway offers Starter, Team and Enterprise plans, billed monthly or yearly.
Every Fernway plan includes two-factor authentication.

claim: Pallas 4 will ship in December 2026.

passages.source: Pallas community forum: Pallas 4 release date?
passages.text: Forum post: I heard from someone at the meetup that Pallas 4 might land around December, no idea if that's true.
Pallas 3.8 was released in August 2026 with improved type inference.
The Pallas team publishes a roadmap but does not commit to release dates.

claim: Driftwood encrypts data at rest.

passages.text: Driftwood syncs folders between your devices in the background.
Every file Driftwood stores is kept AES-256 encrypted on disk on our servers.
Driftwood has clients for macOS, Windows, iOS and Android.

claim: Corvid supports webhooks for payment events.

passages.text: Corvid does not support webhooks yet; poll the /events endpoint to learn about payment events.
Events are retained for 30 days.
Corvid processes card and bank transfer payments in 14 countries.

claim: Corvid sends webhooks for refund events.

passages.text: Corvid webhooks fire for payment events: payment.created, payment.succeeded and payment.failed.
Refunds can be issued from the dashboard or with POST /refunds.
Webhook payloads are signed with HMAC-SHA256.

claim: Pebble's maximum upload size is 5 GB.

passages.text: Single uploads of up to 5 GB are accepted; larger files must use multipart upload.
Pebble stores objects in three availability zones.
Download bandwidth is free for the first 100 GB each month.

claim: Pebble accepts single uploads of up to 50 GB.

passages.text: Single uploads of up to 5 GB are accepted; larger files must use multipart upload.
Pebble stores objects in three availability zones.
Download bandwidth is free for the first 100 GB each month.

claim: Marlin supports HTTP/3.

passages.text: Marlin is a reverse proxy and load balancer written in Go.
Configuration lives in a single TOML file that reloads without downtime.
Marlin can terminate TLS with certificates from Let's Encrypt.
Health checks run every 10 seconds by default.
Version 2 rewrote the routing engine for lower latency.
Marlin serves traffic over HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 (QUIC).
Metrics are exported in Prometheus format on port 9090.

claim: Marlin supports server push over HTTP/3.

passages.text: Marlin serves traffic over HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 (QUIC).
Server push is supported for HTTP/2 connections.
Metrics are exported in Prometheus format on port 9090.

claim: Ostrich's v1 API is still available.

passages.text: The v1 API was shut down on March 1, 2026; every v1 request now returns 410 Gone.
Migrate to v2, which uses cursor pagination.
Ostrich's status page lists all API incidents.

claim: Glimmer is released under the MIT license.

passages.text: Glimmer is open source under the MIT License.
Contributions are welcome; see CONTRIBUTING.md.
Glimmer renders charts to SVG and Canvas.

claim: Tidewater does not collect telemetry.

passages.text: Tidewater sends no usage data or telemetry; nothing leaves your machine.
Tidewater is a local-first note-taking app.
Sync is optional and end-to-end encrypted.

claim: Tidewater does not collect telemetry.

Tidewater is a local-first note-taking app.
Sync is optional and end-to-end encrypted.

claim: Harbor ORM 3.0 supports composite primary keys.

passages.text: Harbor ORM 3.0 adds support for composite primary keys on every database it supports.
Harbor ORM 3.0 drops support for Node.js 18.
Harbor ORM generates TypeScript types from your schema.

claim: Verdigris 1.x supports streaming exports.

passages.text: Streaming exports are supported for every table.
Exports can be written as CSV or Parquet.
Each database is stored as a single SQLite file.
Install with pip install verdigris.

claim: The Lanternfish v1 API returns up to 500 results per page.

passages.text: Each page returns up to 500 results; pass the cursor to fetch the next one.
Authenticate with an API key in the X-Api-Key header.
Webhooks were added in March.

claim: Copperline's Basic plan includes priority support.

passages.text: Includes priority support with a four-hour response time.
Up to five users and 10 GB of storage.
All data is encrypted in transit and at rest.

claim: Ravenmoor Community Edition includes audit logs.

passages.text: Audit logs record every sign-in and permission change for 365 days.
Free to self-host under the AGPL.
Dark mode is now available.
Run the Docker image and open port 8080.

claim: Sablefin Agent supports ARM64.

passages.text: Runs on x86-64 and ARM64 hosts.
Sablefin Agent ships host metrics to the Sablefin cloud.
Billed per host per month.

claim: Thornbury Mobile supports offline mode.

passages.text: Offline mode keeps working without a connection and syncs your changes when you reconnect.
Available for iPhone and iPad.
Version 6 adds tags and nested folders.

claim: Quarrystone 3.0 supports multi-region replication.

passages.text: Supports multi-region replication out of the box.
Pricing is per node per hour.
Create a cluster from the console or the CLI.

claim: Wrenfield's Pro plan includes custom domains.

passages.text: Includes custom domains and password-protected pages.
Sites are served from a wrenfield.site subdomain.
Create a site from a template in under a minute.
We now support image galleries.
